original_record.question:
Which of the figures can be cut into these 3 pieces?
<image1>
<image2>
original_record.subject: combinatorial geometry

image1: left semicircle joined to right-isosceles triangle
image2: C heart with two semicircular lobes and two straight sides

answer_verification.method: The two equal right-isosceles triangles join along hypotenuses into a square. Their leg length equals the semicircle diameters. Keep one semicircle attached to the first triangle and attach the second to the adjacent top square side: exact heartC. Both convex semicircular boundaries must remain external in a nonoverlapping dissection; A has three, D none, E onlyone; diskB cannot include the positive triangle area while retaining the two fixed-radius semicircles as its full boundary.
